titleEn: You May Cry—Wipe with Your Scarf!

pages.text: "I will open it!" Pipo flung open the house door and ran out. Today he wanted to open the pen alone. Farther away, sheep called baa to him at the gate.
The yard had frozen solid overnight. His feet slid—crash! He fell on his bottom on the ice. His knee stung and palms tingled.
Tears almost burst out, but he squeezed both fists. "C-crying is for babies... I will not cry." His voice shook. Holding back made his throat tighten and nose sting.
Mom hurried out of the house. "Pipo, that hurt, did it not?" She knelt to meet his eyes. "You feel like crying. You do not have to hold it back."
She gently rubbed his knee. "Falling hurt and scared you. Then it is all right to cry. Crying is nothing to be ashamed of." Tears filled his eyes.
"Waaah!" He nestled into Mom's arms and cried hard. She wiped his tears with the scarf's tip and sang, "You may cry—wipe with your scarf!"
After a good cry, his tight throat relaxed. "Oh? I feel all right now!" Sniffling, he lifted his face and wiped his eyes with his own scarf tip.
Pipo crouched on the ice, hands at his chest. His knee still hurt a little, but his heart was light. At the gate, sheep called baa to him again.
"One, say it hurts! Two, cry if I want to! Three, wipe with my scarf!" Careful footprints led to the pen. He held the handle in both hands and opened it with a creak.
Sheep hurried out past him. Pipo hugged Mom's neck and nestled close. "A good cry let all the tight feelings out!" Waving his scarf tip, he smiled. "You may cry—wipe with your scarf!"
